title: Water Quality, Alkalinity, pH, EC & Solution Preparation
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for source-water characterization, solution preparation, meter verification and controlled batch acceptance
prerequisites: Sensors, Controllers, Alarms, Calibration & Data Quality or equivalent measurement foundation
evidencePolicy: Course uses controlled university-extension water chemistry, peer-reviewed cannabis source-water evidence, data-integrity and safety references. pH, alkalinity and EC are taught as distinct measurements; source-specific chemistry and research examples are not universal cannabis specifications.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize acid/base handling outside procedure, unapproved formulation changes, chemical mixing beyond assigned work, or batch release outside controlled acceptance/disposition authority.
description: Develops specialist source-water characterization and solution-preparation reasoning across pH, alkalinity, EC, major-ion context, meter quality, recipe execution, batch verification and evidence-based hold/escalation.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate irrigation-water pH, alkalinity, EC and ion composition and explain why no single measurement fully characterizes source-water behavior.
Evaluate source-water variability and risk using sampling history, treatment/source changes, major-ion or contaminant context and appropriate retesting triggers.
Verify pH/EC measurement systems using controlled standards, probe condition, temperature/sample handling and traceable calibration/verification records.

Execute and verify an approved solution-preparation workflow using material identity, recipe version, final volume, ordered additions, mixing and measured acceptance criteria without independently redesigning the formula.
Produce a reconstructable batch/source-water record and apply controlled hold, correction, escalation or disposition logic when verified results fall outside acceptance.
